text:
kim: Heads-up — I kicked off a preflight perf run for the runtime PR (kernel selector change). Wanted to surface results before we flip the canary.

dave: Thanks. Which traces did you run?

kim: Ran the standard suite: short-chat (<=128 tokens), long-chat (1k tokens), batching stress (1-16 concurrent), and embeddings pipe. Scripts in ci/perf/preflight.sh.

sara: Any regressions so far? p50/p95/p99?

kim: Short-chat p50 ~2% faster, p95 ~same, p99 +8ms on average (seen on older nvidia nodes). Long-chat improved token throughput by ~6%. Batching stress shows increased variability at batch sizes >8.

mike: +8ms at p99 is concerning for some SLAs. Can you drop the raw numbers and the job IDs?

kim: Job IDs: perf-17678-short-1, perf-17678-long-1, perf-17678-batch-1. Raw p99 deltas: short: +8ms, long: -12ms, batch at 16: +22ms tail. Uploaded flamegraphs to https://internal.perf/17678/ — see folder kernel-sel.

perf-bot: automated note: Alert rule 'canary-p99' triggered on perf-17678-batch-1 (p99 delta +22ms).

sara: Thanks. @kim, can you run the profiler with cpu/gpu kernel sampling for the batch case? Maybe kernel selection falling back to a slower path at higher sequence lengths.

kim: On it. Spawning gpu-sample job now, will attach perf logs in ~20m. Also re-ran with quantized model variant — tail improved there.

mike: That's interesting — quantized variant helps tail, might indicate kernel memory behavior. If it's a regression only at large batch/long prompts, maybe we can gate the canary to traffic caps and a feature-flag throttle.

dave: For the release decision: we need a mitigation plan + rollback playbook. If quantized variant mitigates, could we auto-fallback to quantized for Dedicated customers during canary?

kim: We can add a fallback to model-quant-fast when batch_sz>8 or seq_len>512. It's a config change and quick to add to routing.

perf-bot: note: canary-window: 30m. Current canary start scheduled in 1h unless held.

sara: Recommend holding until profiler output. If kernel path is unstable we risk customer incidents at p99. But if fallback is straightforward we could proceed with a restricted canary: 10% traffic, batch cap 8, auto-fallback to quantized.

mike: Agreed. Also add tracing hooks for KV cache hit/miss metrics and token latency per-model. Need those to verify in real traffic.

kim: Profiler results uploaded: flamegraph shows fallback into generic GEMM path when batch concurrency hits memory cutoff — kernel selection heuristic misestimates memory for combined kv + activation. I can patch heuristic and push a test.

dave: How long for the patch and a quick validation run?

kim: Patch is small, tests + perf run ~45m. If green, we can update the canary config to: limited routing (10%), batch cap 8, auto-fallback quantized, and enhanced tracing.

sara: Sounds good. @mike please prepare rollback note: command to flip routing back to previous selector and how to disable auto-fallback.

mike: On it — will add step-by-step to runbook and attach to this thread.

kim: I'll hold the canary start and ping when tests finish. If patch fails, we either postpone or run with the restricted config and close monitoring.

perf-bot: automated note: perf-run perf-17678-gpu-sample completed. Attachments: flamegraph.svg, kernel-logs.txt.

kim: Patch pushed to branch runtime/kernel-selector-fix. Triggered CI perf again: perf-17678-patch-1.

dave: Thanks. If perf-17678-patch-1 shows p99 <= baseline+5ms for batch cases, I approve opening the canary with the restricted config.

kim: Will report back in ~50m.

mike: Also tagging @oncall to keep an eye during the restricted canary window.

sara: Nice work. :thumbsup:
